brief:
## The options

| | Viewers | Octave | Build |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) Keep as is | Nothing now. Octave's sign-in screen, the first thing every viewer sees, is tested last, after the whole M1 contract. | Waits for all of JS-216 (catalog, approvals, profile, every example), then JS-184. | No new task. Sign-in waits behind about ten operations it doesn't need. |
| (2) Split JS-216: a sign-in slice, then JS-184 at once, the rest beside | Same as (1) at the end. The screen every viewer meets first gets the most testing. | Mocks sign-in within one task. Tests against a real server one task later. Reads the camelCase rename once, early. | One more task through the workflow (small: three operations and a rename). JS-216's remainder runs beside JS-184. Both edit the contract file, so expect a rebase. |
| (3) Fold sign-in's contract into JS-184 | Same as (2). | No contract to mock until JS-184's own notice. The rename arrives together with working code. | JS-184 grows to a contract change, a rename across every v1 operation and the build. That breaks "one capability per task" and puts the rename's risk on the sign-in's merge. |

## Decision: (2)

- serves: PRODUCT.md, "Signing in is easy and safe"; Goal 3, Octave's features have the server they need; D-132, which publishes each capability with examples before it is served.
- reason: sign-in is the first screen of every app. Octave can test it only against a server. Nothing in it needs the catalog. The contract-first rule (D-132) holds with one small task. Option (3) would give that rule up for nothing.
- Also: Octave can only test against a server it can start. JS-198, which publishes a server with a test account, therefore moves up to run beside it.
tradeoff: One more task through the workflow (small: three operations and a rename). JS-216's remainder runs beside JS-184. Both edit the contract file, so expect a rebase.
serves: PRODUCT.md, "Signing in is easy and safe"; Goal 3, Octave's features have the server they need; D-132, which publishes each capability with examples before it is served.
entry: Sign-in comes first. JS-216 is split: JS-223 makes the contract camelCase and declares sign-in, sign-out and `/me` with examples. JS-184 follows at once and serves them, accepting Bearer and, until the cutover, its token on the Jellyfin routes. JS-198 moves up beside them, so Octave can test against a server it can start. JS-216's remainder runs beside JS-184. Disabling in configuration moves to JS-194. Asked by Octave through the owner: "so they can start testing it sooner".
